forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Sevenoaks budget paper says no expectation that a Section 114 notice will be needed
news_drafts.lead:
Sevenoaks District Council's transition budget report says there is "currently no expectation that the Council would be required to be in that position", referring to the issuing of a Section 114 notice. The report went to the Finance & Investment Advisory Committee on 10 November 2026.

The statement is in the report's legal implications section. That section says that failure to set a balanced budget could lead to a Section 114 notice, the formal notice a council's chief finance officer issues when the council cannot balance its budget. The notice would be issued by the council's Section 151 Officer, its chief finance officer.

The report lists the risks as uncertainty about the size of the shortfall and uncertainty about the timing of the financial settlement. It gives no figure for the shortfall in the material reviewed.

news_drafts.headline: Sevenoaks projects £250k deficit as service costs rise and reserves drain
news_drafts.lead: Sevenoaks Council is forecasting a £250,000 deficit for the year to March 2027, a material shift from its break-even budget after four months of the financial year. Service spending has overrun by £244,000, with particular pressure in planning and regulatory services, partly offset by strong investment returns of £165,000. The council's usable reserves, money set aside for planned spending, have been drawn down by £841,000 in the first four months alone, with the Financial Plan Reserve depleted by 18 per cent. At the current rate, total reserves would fall by approximately £2.5 million over a full year. The deficit includes the impact of a 3.3 per cent pay award still under negotiation, estimated to cost £71,000 beyond budget. The council's treasury management, including investments in multi-asset income funds and a housing loan portfolio, is performing well but cannot fully offset the underlying operational pressures.

findings.paper_title: Financial Monitoring Report - September 26 Appendix B
findings.headline: Direct Services agency spend forecast at £599k against a £344k budget
findings.detail: The salary monitoring table shows Direct Services agency spend of £599k forecast against £344k budgeted, a £255k variance. Finance agency spend is forecast at £155k against nil budget. Overall SDC-funded salaries are forecast £457k under budget.
findings.matters: Agency cover costing more than budgeted while permanent salaries underspend is a staffing pattern finance directors often see in service reviews.
findings.figures: Direct Services agency forecast £599k vs budget £344k (£255k over); Finance agency forecast £155k vs nil; SDC-funded salary forecast £457k under budget

findings.paper_title: Financial Monitoring Report - September 26 Appendix B
findings.headline: 27-37 Swanley High street forecast total project expenditure of £5,911,409 against £6,114,000 approved
findings.detail: The capital dashboard shows the Swanley High Street (meeting point) scheme forecast at £5,911,409 in total against an approved gross cost of £6,114,000, a forecast underspend of £202,591.
findings.matters: A capital scheme delivered under its approved budget is an outcome a finance director elsewhere can compare with their own project delivery.
findings.figures: Approved £6,114,000; forecast total £5,911,409; variance £(202,591) under budget

findings.paper_title: Financial Monitoring Report - September 26 Appendix B
findings.headline: Affordable Housing External Borrowing budgeted at £15,000,000, with £1,500,000 forecast in 2026/27 and nothing spent to end-September
findings.detail: The capital dashboard shows a £15m external borrowing line for affordable housing, with £1.5m forecast in 2026/27 and £1.5m in each of 2027/28 and 2028/29. A memo line records the Quercus Housing £15m over 10 years, with no profiling set.
findings.matters: A new £15m external borrowing commitment with no profiling set is a borrowing decision a lender or peer finance director would want to see the timing of.
findings.figures: Budget £15,000,000; spend to date £0; 2026/27 forecast £1,500,000; memo Quercus Housing £15,000,000 over 10 years
findings.quote: Quercus Housing £15m over 10 years no profiling set

findings.paper_title: Financial Monitoring Report - September 26 Appendix B
findings.headline: Financial Plan reserve falls from £3.1m to £2.6m, a £565k drawdown in the year to end-September
findings.detail: The Financial Plan earmarked reserve opens at £3,127k and stands at £2,562k at end-September. Budget Stabilisation falls by £297k over the same period, from £14,312k to £14,015k.
findings.matters: Drawing on the reserve designed to smooth the budget is the mechanism a finance director would watch as a sign of how long the cushion will last.
findings.figures: Financial Plan £3.1m to £2.6m (£565k drawn); Budget Stabilisation £14.3m to £14.0m (£297k drawn)
findings.quote: BS380 E Earmarked Reserve - Financial Plan

findings.paper_title: Financial Monitoring Report - September 26 Appendix B
findings.headline: Total reserves stand at £32.0m at end-September 2026, up £952k from the £31.0m opening balance
findings.detail: The reserves table shows total reserves rising from £31,023k at the start of 2026/27 to £31,975k at end-September, with General Fund up £200k. Capital Expenditure Reserve and Waste and Recycling Reserve increase over the same period.
findings.matters: Reserves being rebuilt during a year with a forecast deficit is a balance-sheet position that lenders and peer finance officers would track.
findings.figures: Opening total reserves £31.0m; end-September £32.0m; movement £952k increase; General Fund £2.1m to £2.3m
